walkthroughs.body_html:
Stoichiometry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Stoichiometry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Stoichiometry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the fingerprint region (below ~1500 cm^-1) in IR spectroscopy?
options: The fingerprint region is used to identify which functional groups are present.
It is unique to each compound — used to identify a specific molecule by matching to a known spectrum.
The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
